In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the observed suppression of quarkonia and of light hadron photoproduction at high xF in nuclear matter is not due to the energy loss of the partons that participate in the hard subprocess.
the nuclear suppression in quarkonium photoproduction at high xF is a consequence of the nuclear suppression of the gluon distribution at large xF in nuclei.
the observed nuclear suppression in the photoproductions of quarkonia and light hadrons at high xF can only be understood in terms of a modification of the wave function of the produced state.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have shown that the observed nuclear suppression in quarkonium and light-hadron production at high x(F) can only be understood as a result of nuclear effects on the initial parton distribution functions.

the nuclear suppression of quarkonia at high xF is due to the nuclear modification of the initial or the final states, and that no nuclear suppression of the photoproduction cross section is expected at large xF.

the observed nuclear suppression in quarkonium photoproduction and in the photoproduc- tion of light hadrons is not due to the nuclear modification of the parton distribution functions, but rather to the nuclear suppression of the photon flux.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the energy loss of a parton is a non-local operator, and the amount of energy that can be radiated is bounded by the total energy of the parton.

the nuclear suppression of heavy quarkonium production in the high xF region can only be explained in terms either of a modification of the wavefunction of the heavy quark pair in the nucleus, or of a modification of its production cross section.

the observed nuclear suppression in quarkonium and Drell-Yan production at large xF can only be explained by a mechanism that affects the production process itself, such as the formation time of the quarkonium or the coherence length of the Drell-Yan pair.
